title: The diagonal hides more length
hook: Which line can contain the pictured 140cm rod?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: that a rectangle's diagonal is longer than either of its sides, so a thin item too long for the width can still fit corner to corner

misconception: An item longer than the longest wall cannot lie flat in the room.
objective: The rectangle’s diagonal is longer than either edge. A thin rod can fit along it when it is too long for the width; area alone does not answer a length-fit question.

recall.question: A floor is 60 × 80 cm. Can a thin 95 cm rod lie flat on it?
options: No: 95 cm is longer than both sides
Only if the floor's area is large enough
recall.why: The diagonal is √(60² + 80²) = 100 cm, longer than either edge, so a thin 95 cm rod fits along it. Area does not answer a length question, and a thick object is a different problem.
